BiblicalUsage: To crumble, the Aramaic verb for what happens to the image in Nebuchadnezzar's dream, when the stone strikes and the iron, clay, brass, silver, and gold are broken in pieces together and become like chaff. The word stands in Daniel's Aramaic under the root for crushing, the same verb that breaks the kingdoms of the earth.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that every kingdom of man crumbles before the stone cut without hands, and the God who raises the stone is the God who outlasts them all.
